name: Same Yogurt, Different Words
sources: Concepts: framing effect, bundle pricing, scarcity (standard behavioural-economics ideas). All prices and labels are illustrations.

segments.caption: Imagine you're selling yogurt… and nobody's buying.
segments.say: Imagine you're selling yogurt, and nobody is buying.

segments.caption: One cup says 20% fat. The other says 80% fat free.
segments.say: Here's a test. One cup says 20 percent fat. The other says 80 percent fat free. Which one sells?

segments.caption: 80% fat free.
segments.say: Most people grab the 80 percent fat free. It just sounds healthier.

segments.caption: It's the exact same yogurt.
segments.say: But it's the exact same yogurt. People bought the words, not the yogurt. That's the framing effect: how something is said changes how we judge it.

segments.caption: A bag + watch for $49… or a bag for $49 and the watch is FREE?
segments.say: Next. A bag and a watch for 49 dollars. Or a bag for 49 dollars, and the watch is free. Which feels better?

segments.caption: Same price. Same stuff.
segments.say: The free watch, obviously. Same price, same stuff. But free feels like a win. That's bundle pricing.

segments.caption: Now it says only 3 left.
segments.say: Last one. A button says buy now, for 100 dollars. Most people think, I'll get it later. Now it says: only 3 left. Suddenly, you want it right now.

segments.caption: Scarcity. Fear of missing out makes people act fast.
segments.say: That's scarcity. Fear of missing out makes people act fast, before they've really thought.

segments.title: PROTECT YOUR MONEY

items.sub: 'free' is usually built into the price
sleep on it if you can

items.text: Ask: would I buy it at full price?

segments.say: So, protect your money. Flip the label: 80 percent fat free means 20 percent fat. Check what each item really costs, because free is usually built into the price. When you see only 3 left, pause. And ask yourself: would I buy this at full price?

segments.title: SAME PRODUCT
segments.disclaimer: Financial education, not personal advice. Examples are illustrations.
segments.say: The product never changed. Only how it was said. Know the tricks, and spend on purpose. Financial education, not personal advice. Follow for more.
